Engine::resample + ClipResampler: EXACT ALIGNMENT. Output frame count = ceil(frames*out/in) exactly (requested == actual). Alignment derived from rubato 5.0.1 internals (start index -(SINC_LEN-1), trim floor(SINC_LEN*r/2)): rubato leaves the output ahead by 1-frac(128 r) frames (0.4..1.0 measured); the resampler prepends pad_input_frames zeros (smallest s with q | 128+s and non-negative lag) and drops drop_output_frames, giving whole-frame alignment. Pad/drop: 48k->44.1k (32,29), 44.1k->48k (19,20), 32k->48k (2,2), 48k->96k (1,1), 48k->48k (1,0). Impulse test on those five pairs: peak lands on the exact image index, residual offset 0.007..0.010 frames (about the 1/128 sinc-table step). Sinc path retained (no FFT feature, no new deps).

notes.api_notes: Deviations from brief (stronger): Processor::process takes &CancellationToken and returns Result; Processor::accepts/required_sample_rate_hz/max_frames/identity/reset added; Engine owns resource + live revision (RequestContext has no current_revision); BlockReceipt is Copy with labels()/peak()/rms(); HardLimiter::new(rate, channels, HardLimiterParams). Spec declares no Mono/5.1 labels (UNVERIFIED) so ChannelLayout::mono(label) takes the label. Send type is named SendRoute (std Send would be shadowed). ResampleReceipt gained pad_input_frames/drop_output_frames.
limitations: Equalizer shapes follow the W3C Audio EQ Cookbook; Adobe curve parity and spec flags constant_q/low2ndorder/high2ndorder/ultraquiet are not mapped (spec declares no semantics).
Cancel inside Engine::resample is polled only at admission and at the publication gate (rubato process_all is one call; bounded by MAX_BLOCK_FRAMES). Engine::bounce polls between blocks.

Resampler residual alignment 0.007..0.010 frames is a measured value on five rate pairs, not a proof for every pair; pairs whose reduced denominator q needs pad > MAX_BLOCK_FRAMES are rejected with invalid_rate.

RampedGain::reset reverts only an unpublished block; after publication (Processor::commit) reset is a no-op, so a Chain un-bypass or bounce-start reset no longer reverts the last published ramp. Wrappers around a Processor must forward reset and commit (a wrapper that does not forward commit still commits lazily at the next process start).
